mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as higher rates increase discount rates and reduce equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During strong housing market conditions (HOUST > 1600 thousand units), positive S&P 500 forward returns are observed over the next 20 trading days, as housing activity supports consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST > 1600 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) and low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals a tight monetary and labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE < 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A retail sales level above 350,000 million dollars is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as strong consumer spending supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS > 350,000 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 110 (index, 2017=100) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 110 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%), strong payroll growth (PAYEMS > 150k) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as labor market strength supports consumer spending and corporate profits.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS > 150k over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 205) and a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) signals a monetary tightening cycle, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 205 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5% over a 3-year rolling window.
